amendment_2_human_in_the_loop.summary: User direction change: ambiguity must be RESOLVED by the human out loud (stop / go on), not merely declined. Plus user override removing per-motion arm keypress gates.
amendment_2_human_in_the_loop.beat2_ask_now_interactive: After the ask utterance + panel, run_demo captures a spoken reply via listen/transcribe.py (t toggle gives the typed fallback on the same code path) and classifies it with demo/run_demo.py:classify_reply() -- token overlap against two fixed word sets, no LLM. affirmative {go,ahead,yes,yeah,yep,majority,continue,proceed,ok,okay,sure,affirmative,try,anyway,do} -> arm executes task_demo. negative {stop,no,nope,wait,hold,cancel,abort,halt,negative,don't,dont,never} -> arm HOLDS and speaks the new ask_hold template. Reply hitting BOTH sets (e.g. "don't go on") or NEITHER is unrecognized on purpose: robot says it did not understand and re-listens, max 2 retries, then forces typed input. Unclear intent never moves the arm.
amendment_2_human_in_the_loop.beat3_abstain_now_pushes_back: After the refusal the robot listens once more. affirmative ("go on", "try anyway") -> speaks the new abstain_restate template and STILL does not move. negative/unrecognized -> proceeds to BEAT 4. The centerpiece is preserved: being told to try anyway does not make it attempt a task it has zero demonstrations of.
